mil3.3.7:1.2: “Venerable Nāgasena, where eye consciousness arises, there mind consciousness also arises?”
mil3.3.7:1.3: “Yes, Great King, where eye consciousness arises, there mind consciousness also arises.”
mil3.3.7:2.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, does eye consciousness arise first and mind consciousness afterwards, or does mind consciousness arise first and eye consciousness afterwards?”
mil3.3.7:2.2: “Eye consciousness arises first, Great King, and mind consciousness afterwards.”
mil3.3.7:3.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, does eye consciousness command mind consciousness: ‘Arise where I arise’, or does mind consciousness command eye consciousness: ‘Where you will arise, I too will arise’?”
mil3.3.7:3.2: “No, Great King; there is no conversation between them.”
mil3.3.7:4.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that where eye consciousness arises, there mind consciousness also arises?”
mil3.3.7:4.2: “Because of the slope, Great King, because of the doorway, because of habituation, and because of practice.”
mil3.3.7:5.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that, because of the slope, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises?
mil3.3.7:5.3: “What do you think, Great King: when it rains, which way would the water go?”
mil3.3.7:5.4: “It goes, venerable sir, wherever the ground slopes down.”
mil3.3.7:5.5: “Then at a later time, if it rained, which way would that water go?”
mil3.3.7:5.6: “It would go, venerable sir, by the same way that the earlier water went.”
mil3.3.7:6.1: “Great King, does the earlier water command the later water: ‘Go by the way that I go’, or does the later water command the earlier water: ‘By the way that you will go, I too will go’?”
mil3.3.7:6.2: “No, venerable sir; there is no conversation between them; they go because of the slope.”
mil3.3.7:6.3: “In the same way, Great King, because of the slope, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises. Eye consciousness does not command mind consciousness: ‘Arise where I arise’, nor does mind consciousness command eye consciousness: ‘Where you will arise, I too will arise’. There is no conversation between them; they arise because of the slope.”
mil3.3.7:7.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that, because of the doorway, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises?
mil3.3.7:7.3: “What do you think, Great King: suppose a border city of the king had strong ramparts and gateways and a single doorway, and a man wanted to leave it; by which way would he leave?”
mil3.3.7:7.5: “Then another man wanted to leave; by which way would he leave?”
mil3.3.7:7.6: “By the same way that the first man left, venerable sir; he too would leave by that way.”
mil3.3.7:8.1: “Great King, does the first man command the later man: ‘Go by the way that I go’, or does the later man command the first man: ‘By the way that you will go, I too will go’?”
mil3.3.7:8.2: “No, venerable sir; there is no conversation between them; they go because of the doorway.”
mil3.3.7:8.3: “In the same way, Great King, because of the doorway, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises. Eye consciousness does not command mind consciousness: ‘Arise where I arise’, nor does mind consciousness command eye consciousness: ‘Where you will arise, I too will arise’. There is no conversation between them; they arise because of the doorway.”
mil3.3.7:9.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that, because of habituation, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises?
mil3.3.7:9.3: “What do you think, Great King: suppose one cart went first; by which way would the second cart go?”
mil3.3.7:9.4: “By the same way that the first cart went, venerable sir; it too would go by that way.”
mil3.3.7:10.1: “Great King, does the earlier cart command the later cart: ‘Go by the way that I go’, or does the later cart command the earlier cart: ‘By the way that you will go, I too will go’?”
mil3.3.7:10.2: “No, venerable sir; there is no conversation between them; they go because of habituation.”
mil3.3.7:10.3: “In the same way, Great King, because of habituation, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises. Eye consciousness does not command mind consciousness: ‘Arise where I arise’, nor does mind consciousness command eye consciousness: ‘Where you will arise, I too will arise’. There is no conversation between them; they arise because of habituation.”
mil3.3.7:11.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, how is it that, because of practice, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises?
mil3.3.7:11.3: “Just as, Great King, in the crafts of finger-reckoning, counting, calculation, and writing, a beginner is slow, but after some time, through careful practice and regular exercise, he is no longer slow.
mil3.3.7:11.4: In the same way, Great King, because of practice, mind consciousness also arises where eye consciousness arises. Eye consciousness does not command mind consciousness: ‘Arise where I arise’, nor does mind consciousness command eye consciousness: ‘Where you will arise, I too will arise’. There is no conversation between them; they arise because of practice.”
mil3.3.7:12.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, where ear consciousness arises, there mind consciousness also arises …
mil3.3.7:12.2: where nose consciousness arises … where tongue consciousness arises … where body consciousness arises, there mind consciousness also arises?”
mil3.3.7:12.3: “Yes, Great King, where body consciousness arises, there mind consciousness also arises.”
mil3.3.7:13.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, does body consciousness arise first and mind consciousness afterwards, or does mind consciousness arise first and body consciousness afterwards?”
mil3.3.7:13.2: “Body consciousness arises first, Great King, and mind consciousness afterwards.”
mil3.3.7:14.2: There is no conversation between them; they arise because of practice.”
